question: How well is the graph connected, and how accurately can it identify how progress on one disease could help another?

components.note: union-find over all edges except the 5 hypothesis edges, direction ignored

mechanism_links.rule: disease -> mechanism via driven_by, or gene participates_in, or variant_group has_effect, using only edges whose evidence_level is not inferred or hypothesis; two diseases are linked when they reach the same mechanism node; 'specific' excludes loss-of-function, haploinsufficiency, gain-of-function and dominant-negative

bridging_mechanisms.label: Dominant-negative effect (the altered protein blocks the good one)
Gain of function (the protein does too much)
Haploinsufficiency (one working copy is not enough)
Negative regulation of Ras protein signal transduction

design.unit: therapy class x disease; classes: class:aminopyridines = therapy:3-4-diaminopyridine, therapy:amifampridine, therapy:aminopyridine-presynaptic-boost; class:aav-stxbp1 = therapy:aav-stxbp1-gene-replacement, therapy:cap-002; class:aav-slc6a1 = therapy:aav-slc6a1-gene-replacement, therapy:aav9-slc6a1; class:mek-inhibitors = therapy:trametinib, therapy:selumetinib, therapy:mirdametinib, therapy:binimetinib
design.positives: developed_for edges (test cases); study -tests-> therapy + study -studies-> disease pairs are context and, in the extended set, test cases too
design.inclusion: therapy class linked to >= 2 diseases or with >= 1 targets edge
design.hidden_per_case: the held-out developed_for edge(s) of the whole class and every study edge linking the class to the held-out disease
design.candidates: all 45 diseases minus the class's other known diseases (filtered ranking)
design.ties: expected value under random tie-break (rank = better + (tied+1)/2)
design.ci: 95% percentile bootstrap over therapy classes, 2000 draws, seed 20261004
design.weights_fixed_before_running: chain weights 1.0/0.8/0.7; IDF ln((N+1)/(df+1)); combination = phenotype/max + (mechanism+cluster)/max, equal weight

same-family.label: Baseline: same curated family as the known diseases

naive-driven_by.label: Naive rule: target is a driven_by mechanism

hypotheses-rule-no-cluster.label: Current rule without its cluster chain

openai_cross_check.scope: SNARE slice only (biology 62/62 abstracts + community 16); model gpt-6-astra; one model, abstracts only

disagreements: PMID:25381298: atlas files it on vg:SNAP25:missense -> loss-of-function (OpenAI-extracted, unverified); DisMech reads it as dominant-negative
Dravet gene scope: DisMech lists STXBP1 among Dravet genes; the atlas has no STXBP1-Dravet link

g2p_clingen_mechanism_class.rule: for each atlas disease, the G2P / ClinGen-dosage mechanism classes recorded for its MONDO ids (same gene only) vs the atlas: 'strict' = exact class on a driven_by edge; 'lenient' = also effects reached via variant groups, with haploinsufficiency and lysosomal enzyme deficiency counted as loss of function
